reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Four students watched the traffic passing their school for 1 hour.

The table shows what they saw:

| Type of Vehicle | Number |
| :--- | :---: |
| Cars | 60 |
| Bicycles | 30 |
| Buses | 10 |
| Trucks | 20 |

Each student drew a graph to show the results. Which graph shows the results correctly?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four graphical representations of the traffic data:
- Option A: A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. The bars correspond to: Cars = 60 (solid black bar), Bicycles = 30 (light gray bar), Buses = 10 (medium gray bar), Trucks = 20 (white bar with black border).
- Option B: A pictograph with a legend stating '1 wheel = 10 vehicles'. Cars has 5 wheels, Bicycles has 4 wheels, Buses has 1 wheel, and Trucks has 2 wheels.
- Option C: A vertical bar graph with the same axis and colors as Option A, showing: Cars = 60, Bicycles = 30, Buses = 20, Trucks = 10.
- Option D: A pie chart divided into four sectors: Cars covers the right half (180°, solid black). Bicycles covers the bottom-left quadrant (90°, light gray). The remaining top-left quadrant is divided between Buses (a larger sector, medium gray) and Trucks (a smaller sector, white).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
On the map, 1 cm represents 10 km on the land.

[Image: Map showing towns and roads]

On the land, about how far apart are the towns Melville and Folley?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangular map showing three towns marked with dots: Melville near the top center, Mockem on the middle left, and Folley to the lower right. A thick curved black line representing "Red River" runs diagonally across the map from the lower-left to the upper-right. Thin lines represent roads: one goes vertically down through Melville and Mockem, and another connects Melville curving down and to the right, crossing the Red River and passing through Folley. In the bottom right corner of the map, an inset box contains a scale line segment marked with vertical end-ticks labeled "1 cm = 10 km". On the map, the straight-line distance between Melville and Folley is approximately 5 times the length of the 1 cm scale bar.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph below shows the humidity in a room as recorded on a certain morning.

[Image: Graph of Humidity in Room]

On the morning shown in the graph, how many times between 6 a.m. and 12 noon was the humidity exactly 20 percent?
reference_items.figure_description: A line graph titled "Humidity in Room". The vertical axis is labeled "Percent Humidity" with horizontal grid lines and markings at 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50. The horizontal axis is labeled "Time (a.m.) in hours" with vertical grid lines and markings at 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 noon. A continuous curve starts at (6, 5), rises through (7, 20) to a peak at (8, 40), then decreases passing through (9, 30) and (10, 20) to a minimum of about 14 between 10 and 11, then rises passing 20 between 11 and 12, reaching 25 at 12 noon. The curve intersects the horizontal line for 20 percent humidity at three points: at 7 a.m., at 10 a.m., and between 11 a.m. and 12 noon.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three geometric figures composed of small congruent right triangles:
- Figure 1: A single square with a diagonal line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, dividing it into two right triangles labeled '1' (top-left) and '2' (bottom-right). Below the square is the label 'Figure 1'.
- Figure 2: A square divided into a 2-by-2 grid of 4 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 8 congruent triangles numbered 1 through 8: top-left square has 1 (upper) and 2 (lower); top-right square has 3 (upper) and 4 (lower); bottom-left square has 5 (upper) and 6 (lower); bottom-right square has 7 (upper) and 8 (lower). Below is the label 'Figure 2'.
- Figure 3: A square divided into a 3-by-3 grid of 9 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 18 congruent triangles. None of the triangles are numbered. Below is the label 'Figure 3'.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
